frs_sections.title: OVERVIEW
frs_sections.content:
A2B replaces the bulky, heavy point-to-point analog and digital audio wiring
harnesses of a vehicle with a single twisted-pair daisy-chain. Where a
conventional automotive audio system runs many shielded cables from a head unit
to each microphone, amplifier, and speaker, A2B runs one unshielded twisted
pair from node to node in a line, carrying audio, control, interrupts, and power
together.

The bus is mastered by a single A2B main node (the A2B master). The main node
is connected to the vehicle host processor / SoC through a local I2S/TDM audio
port and a local I2C control port. The main node A2B transceiver converts the
host's local I2S/TDM audio frames and I2C register traffic into the A2B line
protocol and transmits them downstream over the twisted pair to the first sub
node. Each A2B…

frs_sections.title: NODE DISCOVERY AND ADDRESSING
The host, through the main node, initiates discovery of the next undiscovered
frs_sections.content:

  3. The newly powered sub node achieves bus lock (phase-locks to the recovered
     bus clock and superframe sync) and announces itself.
  4. The main node assigns the sub node a node address (its position index in
     the chain, 0..9) and reads its node identification / vendor / product
     registers.
  5. The host configures the newly discovered node's audio slots, I2S/TDM
     format, I2C passthrough, GPIO, and interrupts by writing its registers
     (tunneled over the bus).

frs_sections.content:

Node addressing: each sub node is identified by its node address, which equals
its position in the daisy chain (0 for the node nearest the main node, up to 9).
The main node addresses control and register traffic to a specific sub node by
node address; broadcast addressing to all nodes is also supported for common
configuration. Audio slots are mapped to nodes by configuration during/after
discovery.

Discovery is deterministic and ordered because phantom power is applied
segment-by-segment: a downstream node cannot be discovered until its upstream
neighbor has been discovered and instructed to switch power to the next segment.

frs_sections.title: TUNNELED I2S / TDM AUDIO, I2C CONTROL, GPIO, AND INTERRUPTS
frs_sections.content:
A2B does not invent new local audio or control formats. Instead it tunnels the
familiar local interfaces transparently across the bus:

  - I2S / TDM audio tunneling: each A2B transceiver has a local I2S/TDM port
    (BCLK, SYNC/FSYNC/WS, DTX/DRX, with TDM slot framing). Audio presented to a
    node's local I2S/TDM input is mapped into A2B downstream or upstream slots,
    carried across the bus, and presented at the destination node's local
    I2S/TDM output. The local I2S/TDM clocks at each node are generated by the
    A2B transceiver and are synchronous to the bus, so all nodes' audio is
    sample-aligned.

  - I2C control tunneling: the host's I2C bus (connected to the main node's
    local I2C port) is tunneled over the A2B line so the host can read/write the

frs_sections.title: CLOCKING, LOCK, AND RE-TIMING
frs_sections.content:
The main node is the timing master. It generates the bus clock and the
superframe SYNC. Each sub node recovers the bus clock from its upstream twisted
pair, phase-locks to it, and regenerates a clean, re-timed signal toward its
downstream neighbor. This node-by-node re-timing is what allows the chain to span
a long total cable length without accumulating jitter: each node restores the
signal.

All local I2S/TDM clocks (BCLK and SYNC/FSYNC) at every node are derived from the
recovered bus clock, so the entire system shares one audio time base. A node
reports a loss-of-lock condition as an interrupt to the main node.

Bus lock sequence at a node: detect activity on the B-side twisted pair →
recover clock → achieve superframe lock (align to SYNC) → respond to discovery →

frs_sections.title: DATA INTEGRITY, ERRORS, AND DIAGNOSTICS
frs_sections.content:
A2B is designed for the automotive environment and includes line diagnostics:
  - Per-node and per-line error detection (for example data decoding errors,
    CRC on the control/superframe structure, bus-lock errors).
  - Line fault diagnostics: detection of cable open, cable short to ground, short
    to battery, short across the pair, and reversed wiring on a given segment,
    reported through interrupt status registers.
  - Phantom-power fault detection (over-current / under-voltage) per segment.
  - Interrupt-driven reporting of all of the above upstream to the main node and
    then to the host.

These diagnostics let the host localize a fault to a specific segment / node,
which is essential for serviceability of a vehicle audio harness.

frs_sections.title: APPLICATION EXAMPLES
frs_sections.content:
- Microphone arrays: multiple remote microphone nodes (for hands-free, voice
    recognition, in-car communication, ANC/RNC) stream upstream audio to the
    head unit over one twisted pair, drawing phantom power from the bus.
  - Amplifiers / speakers: downstream audio channels are delivered to remote
    smart-amplifier nodes near the speakers, removing long analog speaker-level
    runs from the harness.
  - Active / road noise cancellation (ANC / RNC): the deterministic low latency
    and sample-aligned multichannel audio of A2B make it suitable for distributed
    ANC/RNC where reference microphones, error microphones, and anti-noise
    amplifiers are on different nodes.

frs_sections.title: SUMMARY
frs_sections.content:
A2B (Automotive Audio Bus, Analog Devices AD24xx) carries multichannel digital
audio, I2C control, GPIO, interrupts, AND phantom power over a single unshielded
twisted pair in a daisy chain of one main node (master) plus up to ten sub nodes
(slaves). It uses node discovery and addressing, a sample-rate-locked superframe
with downstream and upstream regions for deterministic low latency, and tunnels
the local I2S/TDM audio and I2C control of each node transparently across the
bus. Each node is an A2B transceiver such as the AD2410 or an AD242x device.
This combination — single-twisted-pair daisy chain, main/sub node discovery,
superframe, phantom power, and I2S/TDM + I2C tunneling — is the complete and
distinguishing structural definition of the Automotive Audio Bus.

compliance_requirements: All devices on the bus must use open-drain or open-collector outputs (except Ultra Fast-mode which is push-pull unidirectional).
Pull-up resistor to VDD on both SDA and SCL.
Data on SDA must remain stable while SCL is HIGH.
Only master generates START, STOP, repeated START.
Each byte is 8 bits + 1 ACK bit; total 9 SCL clock pulses per byte.
Bus capacitance must not exceed the per-mode maximum (e.g. 400 pF for Standard-mode, 550 pF max with current-source for Hs-mode 400 pF).

functional_requirements.text: A2B shall distribute multichannel digital audio, control data, and power over a single unshielded twisted pair (UTP) in a daisy-chain (line) topology.

An A2B bus shall consist of exactly one A2B main node (master) plus up to ten A2B sub nodes (slaves) daisy-chained in a line; each twisted-pair segment is point-to-point between two adjacent transceivers.
The A2B main node shall connect to the host SoC through a local I2S/TDM audio port and a local I2C control port, and shall act as the bus timing master generating the bus clock and superframe sync.

The bus shall be brought up by a node-discovery process that enumerates sub nodes one at a time, in order, from the node nearest the main node outward, switching phantom power onto each next segment as part of the sequence.
Each sub node shall be identified by a node address equal to its position in the daisy chain (0 nearest the main node, up to 9); broadcast addressing to all nodes shall be supported.

All bus traffic shall be organized into a periodic superframe transmitted once per audio sample period (superframe rate = sample rate, e.g. 48 kHz), containing a synchronization / control region, a downstream portion, and an upstream portion.

Because the superframe is locked to the sample rate and slot positions are fixed by configuration, end-to-end audio latency shall be deterministic, low, and constant — approximately two audio samples.

The main node (and configured intermediate sub nodes) shall be able to supply DC phantom power (bus power) to downstream nodes over the same twisted pair that carries the audio, switched segment-by-segment during discovery.

Each node shall tunnel its local I2S/TDM audio (BCLK, SYNC, DTX/DRX, TDM slots) transparently over the bus, with all nodes' local I2S/TDM clocks derived from the recovered bus clock so audio is sample-aligned.

The host's I2C bus (on the main node's local I2C port) shall be tunneled over the A2B line so the host can read/write the registers of any sub node transceiver and any sub-node-local I2C peripheral; the sub node acts as an I2C controller on its local I2C bus on behalf of the host.

Sub-node local GPIO pin states shall be transportable over the bus (GPIO over distance), and sub-node interrupts shall be tunneled upstream to the main node, which presents a single interrupt to the host.

Each sub node shall recover the bus clock from its upstream twisted pair, phase-lock to it, and regenerate a re-timed signal toward its downstream neighbor so the chain can span a long total cable length without jitter buildup.

A2B shall provide line diagnostics: detection of cable open, short to ground, short to battery, short across the pair, and reversed wiring per segment, plus phantom-power faults, reported upstream to the main node via interrupt status.
Each A2B node shall be built around an A2B transceiver IC (AD24xx family — AD2410 / AD2420 / AD2425 / AD242x); main and sub nodes typically use the same silicon configured into main or sub mode.

error_response_conditions: Loss of bus lock at a node — breaks the chain downstream of that node; reported upstream to the main node as an interrupt.
Line fault on a segment (open / short to ground / short to battery / short across pair / reversed wiring) — detected and reported via interrupt status so the host can localize the fault to a segment.
Phantom-power fault (over-current / under-voltage) on a segment — reported per segment; affected downstream nodes lose power.
Data decoding / CRC error on the superframe control structure — reported via interrupt status.
Discovery failure (next node fails to lock or respond after power is switched on) — discovery halts and is reported to the host.

configurations.name: Main node (master) mode
configurations.description: Transceiver strapped/configured as the bus timing master, bridging the host SoC's local I2S/TDM + I2C to the A2B line; only an A-side (downstream).

configurations.name: Sub node (slave) mode
configurations.description: Transceiver configured as a sub node: B-side upstream toward the main node, A-side downstream toward the next sub node; exposes local I2S/TDM + I2C + GPIO.

configurations.name: Bus-powered (phantom power) node
configurations.description: Sub node drawing all of its power from the A2B line; no local supply.

configurations.name: Local-powered node
configurations.description: Sub node with its own supply, used where the bus cannot deliver enough power.

protocol_overview.type: Single-twisted-pair daisy-chain digital audio bus distributing multichannel audio + I2C control + GPIO/interrupts + power; one main node (master) plus up to ten sub nodes (slaves); synchronous superframe locked to the audio sample rate.
protocol_overview.duplex: bidirectional — each superframe carries a downstream portion (main→subs) and an upstream portion (subs→main)
protocol_overview.topology: daisy chain (line) over a single unshielded twisted pair
protocol_overview.timing_master: the A2B main node generates the bus clock and superframe sync; every sub node phase-locks to it
protocol_overview.medium: single unshielded twisted pair (UTP), ~100 Ω, point-to-point per segment; ~15 m per segment, ~40 m total chain
protocol_overview.superframe_rate: equals the audio sample rate (SYNC rate), e.g. 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz; one superframe per sample period
protocol_overview.latency: deterministic, low, constant — approximately two audio samples end to end
protocol_overview.power: phantom power (bus power) delivered to downstream nodes over the same twisted pair that carries the audio
